_buildFilesNote: build.files: do NOT reintroduce '!node_modules/**/*' plus a hand-picked allowlist. That is exactly what shipped an installed app that died on launch with "Cannot find module 'debug'" - the allowlist named 18 packages, npm hoists transitive dependencies to top-level node_modules, and the exclusion stripped every one it did not name, leaving 211 of 229 production packages out of the asar. electron-builder resolves the real production tree itself and already omits devDependencies, so the correct configuration is to not fight it. Only renderer-only libraries are excluded, because Vite bundles them into build/ and nothing in electron/ or server/ requires them. Note this key lives here and not inside 'build' because electron-builder validates that object strictly and rejects unknown keys. See RAMA_AGI_MASTER_SPEC.md Section 48.
_extraResourcesNote: ai_backend MUST stay in build.extraResources. It was omitted, so an installed Rama had no engine directory at all and StockMind reported 'ai_backend directory not found' on every request - resolveBackendPath() looks in resourcesPath/ai_backend first and there was nothing to find. It is extraResources rather than files because Python is spawned as a child process and cannot be read from inside app.asar. Excluded: __pycache__ and .venv are machine-specific and would not run on another CPU; data/ holds fetched bars and trained models, which are master's and belong in userData rather than baked into an installer; tests/ is not needed at runtime. This note lives at top level, NOT inside build, because electron-builder validates that object strictly and rejects unknown keys - the same reason _buildFilesNote is here. See RAMA_AGI_MASTER_SPEC.md Section 98.
_nativeRebuildNote: DO NOT RUN `npm ci` ON THIS MACHINE. It fails, and because `ci` deletes node_modules BEFORE installing, a failure leaves you with an empty tree and no way back except a network reinstall. Measured: `ci` runs `node-gyp rebuild` for node-pty unconditionally and treats the failure as fatal. The failure is real - Visual Studio 18.7.11919.86 IS installed but WITHOUT the 'Desktop development with C++' workload, so VC/Tools/MSVC is empty, there is no cl.exe, and vswhere returns nothing for Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64. Both node-gyp 9.4.1 and node-gyp 11 refuse correctly; this is not a detection bug, there is genuinely no compiler. BUT NO COMPILER IS NEEDED AT RUNTIME: argon2 0.43.0 installs via node-gyp-build and ships prebuilds/win32-x64/argon2.glibc.node, and node-pty 1.0.0 loads without a local build - both `require()` successfully with zero .node files built. So the gyp step is ceremony here, and only `ci` makes it fatal. TO RESTORE A BROKEN TREE: `npm install --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` (669 packages in about 21 seconds, exact pinned versions from package-lock.json). NOTE ON THE WORDING: this note may not contain a tilde or caret followed by a digit. verifyChartSessions.mjs and verifyMarketClock.mjs both assert package.json holds no version range by testing the WHOLE FILE for that pattern, so an abbreviation like a tilde before a number of seconds trips a real dependency guard from inside a prose comment. Spell durations out, THEN `node node_modules/electron/install.js` to fetch the Electron binary, which --ignore-scripts skips and without which `npm start` cannot launch. `npm run verify` and `npm run build` need neither the compiler nor the Electron binary. `npm run verify:render` needs no playwright download either - it drives the system Edge through playwright's msedge channel. If the C++ workload is ever added, `npm ci` should start working; until then use `npm install`, which is incremental and cannot empty the tree.
